title: Reserve Margin — Editor Intro
summary: Opening splash links rocket reserve and water reserve as the same hard idea: safety means carrying or withholding something useful now because the future is uncertain.
panelPlan: Full-page opening/title composition built from two tactile working surfaces in one coherent room: a rocket fuel/mass ledger and a basin allocation ledger, each with a visible margin that cannot be spent twice.
Use physical gauges, pencil marks, paper and ordinary equipment rather than infographic graphics. The same visual gap should read as both reserve fuel and reserved water.
Do not show the historical ledgers that prove earlier decline, premium-contract exemptions, industrial tankers, public evidence or any later Issue 5 finding.
Give RESERVE SOUNDS LIKE ABUNDANCE and IT IS USUALLY THE OPPOSITE a strong opening hierarchy, then land on the issue title.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: On a rocket, reserve is fuel you carry instead of payload.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: In a basin, reserve is water somebody does not use today.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Public Sky has rules for who can act, how much can move, and when the system must stop.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: None of those rules can tell you how cautious is cautious enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Somewhere between wasting what you have and spending what you cannot replace, somebody has to choose what uncertainty costs.

directionInline.text: Non-diegetic opening title page. Preserve exact caption text. It should frame the issue's tradeoff before evidence assigns any cause. Do not imply that Public Sky caused or did not cause the shortage, and do not reveal any investigation, Tethergrid forecast, allocation decision or flight result.
